title: Minimum Operations to Form Subsequence With Target Sum
summary: Given a 0-indexed array nums consisting of non-negative powers of 2 and an integer target, you need to determine the minimum number of operations required to form a subsequence of nums that sums to the target.
statement: Given a 0-indexed array nums consisting of non-negative powers of 2 and an integer target, you need to determine the minimum number of operations required to form a subsequence of nums that sums to the target. An operation consists of selecting any element nums[i] where nums[i] > 1, removing it from the array, and then adding two occurrences of nums[i] / 2 to the end of the array. If it is impossible to form such a subsequence, return -1.
constraints: Every nums value is a positive power of two.
One operation replaces 2^b by two copies of 2^(b-1); form target from a subsequence.
reference_solution:
def minimum_power_splits(nums,target):
    if sum(nums)<target:return -1
    counts=[0]*32
    for value in nums:counts[value.bit_length()-1]+=1
    operations=0
    for bit in range(31):
        if target>>bit&1:
            if counts[bit]:counts[bit]-=1
            else:
                higher=bit+1
                while higher<32 and not counts[higher]:higher+=1
                if higher==32:return -1
                while higher>bit:
                    counts[higher]-=1;counts[higher-1]+=2;operations+=1;higher-=1
                counts[bit]-=1
        counts[bit+1]+=counts[bit]//2
    return operations

hints: Process target bits low to high because excess small powers can combine freely, while a missing bit requires splitting the nearest larger power.
Count powers by exponent and greedily satisfy each target bit.
Borrow the first higher count, split downward one level at a time, then carry unused pairs upward.
Borrowing any farther power costs more, and lower decisions cannot benefit from postponing an available exact bit.
